interest.page: Marimekko Financial Statements Bulletin 2025 (Nasdaq release 1419594, 2026-02-12), sources/MEKKO.HE_2025-Q4_financial-statement-release_2026-02-12_en_a0.pdf, and the audited Annual report 2025 p.26, CONSOLIDATED CASH FLOW STATEMENT, 1-12/2025 column: beneath the subtotal 'Cash flow from operating activities before financial items and taxes 41.4' the statement prints 'Paid interest and payments on other financial expenses -1.3', 'Interest received and payments on other financial income 0.5' and 'Taxes paid -6.1', and only then 'CASH FLOW FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES 34.5'. Both interest sides are INSIDE the operating total, which is struck after them. The two are printed SEPARATELY, so E18 governs: the halves are entered and the store subtracts

items.non_controlling_interests: not a bridge item — E105 deducts the dividends PAID to minorities in the FLOW, and declines to value the stake as a liability (a second unaudited lever, E29's ground)

bridge.note: borrowings 0 + 0 + leases 0 -- the IFRS 16 liability 30 LEAVES net debt whole (E117: its cash is in the flow; one lessee model, no split) + pension deficit 0 (E35.1) + asset retirement obligations 0 (E68) + prepaid delivery obligations 0 (E81) - cash 37 - other current financial assets DATA MISSING, so nothing is subtracted for them: omitting an ASSET raises net debt and lowers the value, which is the safe direction. No NCI, associate, preferred or convertible leg exists in this schema (E35); a separately presented pension ASSET is not netted (E35.1). Capex legs: combined: capex_combined, the one line the issuer prints

inputs.name: operating_cash_flow
inputs.provenance: AUDITED ANNUAL REPORT 2025, PDF page 86 (printed folio 86), 'Consolidated cash flow statement' under 'Consolidated financial statements, IFRS', 1-12/2025 column: 'CASH FLOW FROM OPERATING ACTIVITIES 34.5 29.1'. AFTER tax ('Taxes paid -6.1' inside the section) and AFTER both interest sides -- the total is struck BELOW 'Paid interest and payments on other financial expenses -1.3' and 'Interest received and payments on other financial income 0.5', which is what interest_in_ocf: yes rests on. SECOND DOCUMENT: the Financial Statements Bulletin 2025, PDF page 26 (printed '26 (35)'), CONSOLIDATED CASH FLOW STATEMENT, prints the same line with the same two figures. The directors' report repeats it per share: 'cash flow from operating activities was EUR 34.5 million (29.1), or EUR 0.85 per share (0.72)'. PAGE REFERENCE CORRECTED 2026-09-08 at the owner's read-back: it named the Bulletin while the entry's `document` and `url` name the audited annual report, and a page reference must point into the document the entry claims

inputs.name: diluted_weighted_average_shares
inputs.provenance: AUDITED ANNUAL REPORT 2025, PDF page 31 (printed folio 31), 'Per-share key figures' in the Report of the Board of Directors: 'Share issue adjusted average number of shares 40,571,380 40,571,380 40,571,380' for 2025, 2024 and 2023, with 'Share issue adjusted number of shares at the end of the period' the SAME 40,571,380 -- the average equals the period-end count because no share was issued or cancelled. THE SAME DOCUMENT STATES IT AGAIN AT ITS OWN PRECISION on PDF page 96 (printed folio 96), note 10 EARNINGS PER SHARE, inside the audited consolidated financial statements: 'Net result for the period, EUR million 24.4 24.4 / Weighted average number of shares, 1,000,000 40.6 40.6 / Basic and diluted earnings per share, EUR 0.60 0.60'. BASIC AND DILUTED ARE ONE COUNT (E38), which is why a diluted field takes a figure the report labels only 'average': note 10's own row is headed 'Basic and diluted earnings per share' and the accounting principles state 'There are no potential shares outstanding at the moment', so there is no dilution to add and the stated average IS the diluted average. It reconciles: 24.4 / 40.571 = 0.601, the printed EPS of 0.60. VERIFIED same_page and NOT cross_document -- p.31 and p.96 are two pages of ONE filing, which the owner ruled at the read-back of 2026-09-08. PDF page numbers added at that read-back: the reference named the tables but no page, and a page reference that names no page is weak

inputs.name: financial_liabilities_noncurrent

CONFIRMED BY THE ISSUER'S OWN KEY FIGURE: the annual report's five-year table prints 'Interest-bearing liabilities, EUR million 29.7', which is 21.5 + 8.2 exactly -- so what Marimekko itself calls its interest-bearing liabilities IS the lease, and there are no borrowings beside it. The unused committed credit lines of EUR 22.4 million are a facility, not a drawing

inputs.name: pension_deficit
inputs.provenance: E107 SEARCHED ABSENCE. Document: sources/MEKKO.HE_2025-FY_annual-financial-report_2026-03-18_en_a0.pdf (552,801 characters of extracted text), searched 2026-09-08 for 'defined benefit' and 'defined-benefit': ZERO occurrences of either. 'pension' occurs 24 times and every one is either a Finnish pension INSURANCE COMPANY on the shareholder register (Ilmarinen 4.87%, Varma 4.75%, Elo 1.94%) or the remuneration note's sentence, 'Pension benefits include only statutory pension payments. The management does not have additional pension benefits.' Finnish statutory TyEL is a contribution arrangement. No defined-benefit obligation exists and no balance sheet in the five documents presents a pension caption

inputs.name: asset_retirement_obligation
inputs.provenance: E107 SEARCHED ABSENCE. Document: the audited annual report (552,801 characters), searched 2026-09-08 for 'asset retirement', 'decommission', 'dismantl', 'restoration', 'make good', 'dilapidation' and 'restoring': TWO hits across the seven terms and BOTH are sustainability boilerplate -- 'the protection and restoration of biodiversity and ecosystems' (EU taxonomy objectives) and Better Cotton 'protecting and restoring the environment'. Neither is an obligation. E68.1: a clothing and homeware designer that LEASES its stores, on none of the refuse-until-read lists. The balance sheet presents no provision caption at all -- 'current provisions' appears in this report only inside the printed FORMULA for net working capital

inputs.name: prepaid_delivery_obligation

fcf_reported.page: E103 REFERENCE FIGURE -- compared against section 5's own construction and NEVER used to build one; the section 5 gate refuses if it ever reaches a basis. Annual report, Report of the Board of Directors, Cash flow and financing: 'Cash flow before cash flow from financing activities in the financial year was EUR 31.6 million (26.8).' NAMED EXACTLY BECAUSE IT IS NOT CALLED FREE CASH FLOW: Marimekko publishes no line under that name. The construction is the same one Bouvet calls net free cash flow -- operating cash flow plus investing cash flow, 34.5 - 2.9 = 31.6 -- and it is NOT E34's: it deducts no share-based compensation and adds back no interest, because both interest sides are already inside its operating total. HAND-READ 2026-09-08; E103's automatic model route could not run on this host (no VSS_OPENROUTER_KEY)

lease.page: FRAMEWORK-EDITS E70, applied 2026-09-08 to an IFRS 16 filer IFRS 16.50(b): a lessee classifies cash payments for the principal portion of the lease liability within FINANCING, and Marimekko prints it there -- p.27 of the same document, CASH FLOW FROM FINANCING ACTIVITIES, 'Payments of lease liabilities -8.7', below the operating total. The operating cash flow never bore the principal, so nothing is added back; the lease is counted once, in net debt (E35, E65)
